nodes.name: Magnetron Sputtering Cu-Zn Alloy Layer
nodes.procedure: The multicomponent Cu-Zn alloy layer was constructed on Zn foil by magnetron sputtering (MS) using the CuZn₅ alloy as the target. In the MS process, Cu and Zn atoms were sputtered and gathered at random on the surface of bare Zn substrate to form various types of Cu-Zn alloys (CuZn, CuZn₅, Cu, Zn, CuZn₂ and Cu₅Zn₈ phases). The optimized sputtering time of 30 min was used to achieve optimal thickness (~7 μm) and electrochemical performance.

nodes.characterization_summary: Uniform, smooth and dense Cu-Zn alloy layer with thickness of about 7 μm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The cross-sectional SEM images reveal that the thickness of the homogeneous Cu-Zn coating layer is about 7 μm (Figure 2d and Figure 2e).

nodes.characterization_summary: Cu and Zn elements are homogeneously distributed demonstrating excellent uniformity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The EDS mapping shows that the Cu and Zn elements are homogeneously distributed, demonstrating an excellent uniformity of Cu-Zn alloy layer (Figure 2c).

As shown in Figure 2g-l, the lattice fringes with lattice spacings of 0.17 nm, 0.238 nm, 0.208 nm, 0.247 nm, 0.189 nm and 0.255 nm are observed, which are corresponding to planes of the CuZn (111), CuZn5 (111), Cu (110), Zn (002), CuZn2 (410) and Cu5Zn8 (222), respectively.
